episodes.207710: A slow moving upper level low pressure system moved down the California coast, tapping ample moisture and spreading precipitation across the state of Arizona.  This was a relatively warm storm with high snow levels, at or above 6500-7000 feet.  Dynamic support and wind shear with this storm led to some severe thunderstorms.  Heavy rain falling over ground saturated from the previous weekend's storm led to flash flooding and elevated creek flows.
episodes.208023: A surface low drifted southeastward from Missouri through Southern Illinois and Western Kentucky during the evening hours of the 18th. Areas to the south with some afternoon clearing allowed for instability to develop, resulting in the formation of multiple clusters of storms that tracked southeastward. The most prominent of these clusters strengthened in far Southeast Missouri, moving across the Mississippi River into far Western Kentucky, at times developing embedded supercell structure. This cluster produced a tornado in Fulton County which tracked southeastward from KY-94 to KY-166 near the Tennessee border, breaking multiple power polls along the way. Effective bulk shear peaked at around 50kts near the Missouri/Kentucky border with DCAPE of 800J/kg to go along with the MLCAPE of over 1000J/kg. Precipitable water peaked at 1.3in.
episodes.208024: A surface low drifted southeastward from Missouri through Southern Illinois and Western Kentucky during the evening hours of the 18th. Areas to the south with some afternoon clearing allowed for instability to develop, resulting in the formation of multiple clusters of storms that tracked southeastward. The most prominent of these clusters strengthened in far Southeast Missouri, moving across the Mississippi River into far Western Kentucky, at times developing embedded supercell structure. This cluster produced hail in Scott City but peaked near and just across the Mississippi River, producing a 61mph wind gust at Dorena. Effective bulk shear peaked at around 50kts near the Missouri/Kentucky border with DCAPE of 800J/kg to go along with the MLCAPE of over 1000J/kg. Precipitable water peaked at 1.3in.
episodes.208533: Between the evening of November 17th and the evening of the 20th, a slow-moving upper-level low pressure system progressed through the Desert Southwest. The combination of the strong dynamical forcing from the low and well-above normal moisture values (PWATs of 0.80+) led to multiple rounds of scattered to widespread moderate to heavy rainfall and isolated thunderstorms. Most of the rain and impacts fell/occurred on the 18th and 19th, with much of central Arizona receiving rainfall totals of 1.00-2.50 and some areas receiving 3+ inches. This rainfall led to instances of flash flooding and flows in normally dry creeks and washes. Several streamflow gauges across the Flood Control District of Maricopa County's (FCDMC) network exceeded designated alarm stages and a couple gauges in far north Phoenix reached bank full. Several swift water rescues as well as road closures were reported across in or near the washes that exceeded alarm stage/bank full. ||With just enough instability (CAPE values near 500 J/KG) and high wind shear (>50 kts), several severe thunderstorms developed, including a few supercells, in Maricopa County on both the 18th and 19th. Hail was the primary severe weather impact, given the lower freezing levels. There was one report of severe hail (1+ inch in diameter) on the 18th, in Sun City Festival, and multiple reports of quarter size to golf ball size hail on the 19th, in Ahwatukee and Tempe. There was also a lot of accumulating hail, especially on the 19th when a portion of I-10 in Tolleson was covered in several inches of hail. The accumulating hail may have been a contributing factor to a partial roof collapse at Desert Sky Mall.||In addition to the flooding and hail, there were also a few reports of funnel clouds and an EF-0 tornado briefly touched down in Forepaugh, AZ, along US-60 between Aguila and Wickenburg during the afternoon hours on the 18th. The tornado caused a small amount of damage, including flipping an RV trailer.
episodes.208759: A strong thunderstorm moved northeast across the parts of the NW Tucson Metro including Oro Valley. This storm had varying hail sizes from pea (0.25 inch diameter) to nickel (0.88 inch diameter) lasting for roughly 5 minutes and caused no damage.
episodes.208765: A mid-level shortwave moved across the middle Mississippi Valley and into the lower Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening of November 18, 2025. Meanwhile, a surface low tracked from northern Missouri into western Kentucky. The associated cold front pushed into northwest Tennessee during the evening hours. A few thunderstorms developed and became severe as the front intersected an instability axis over northwest Tennessee. These severe storms produced large hail over northwest Tennessee.

events.narrative: Eagle Eye Road closed due to flooding of several low water crossings. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Stream Gauge along Tiger Wash just upstream measured water levels exceeding the alarm stage level of 5.9 feet, peaking at 6.02 feet (563 cfs). Timing was based on the time water levels exceeded the alarm stage level. No damages or injuries reported.
Recorded measurement from personal weather station EW4994 Dorena as thunderstorms tracked southeastward through southern Mississippi County.

A water rescue was reported in the area if 421st Ave and Narramore Rd. Multiple rounds of rain fell during the morning and early afternoon, with 1.00-1.50 inches of radar estimated rainfall within the Centennial Wash basin just upstream of the reported rescue. No damages or injuries reported.

A narrow EF-1 tornado (peak winds of 100mph) began on KY-94 just east of Hickman. The tornado then slowly moved southeast, mostly across open fields, doing sporadic minor tree damage before snapping 3 power poles along and near KY-166. The tornado ended near Rice Lane south of KY-166. Photos from the event show a very narrow funnel consistent with the narrow damage path.
Hail measured to quarter size was reported south of Cayce as a supercell storm tracked southeastward towards Tennessee.
Quarter-sized hail fell along Coca Cola Smith Road.
Half-dollar-sized hail fell along Haygood Road.
Water rescue reported in the area of Eagle Eye Rd and Salome Rd due to excessive runoff from Tiger Wash. No injuries reported.
Quarter-sized hail fell on Henry Midway Road.
A USGS stream gauge at Fossil Creek near Strawberry (FCSA3) reported a 3.17 foot rise due to widespread rain across the basin.  Peak flow was 2701 cfs.
Nickel sized hail lasted for approximately 5 minutes, covered the ground, and caused no damage.
Multiple photos and videos of a brief cold air funnel cloud as seen from Surprise and Wittman areas. Timing and location based on radar.
